predecessors.name: Habsburg monarchy
predecessors.text: the Habsburg lands as they stood after the Peace of Pressburg; the page dates the empire's 'Proclamation: 11 August 1804'

successors.name: Austria-Hungary
successors.text: the empire at the Compromise of 1867 (Cliopatria's Austria-Hungary row starts in 1868)

ledger.x: 1806: the Austrian Empire begins in Cliopatria's row after the Peace of Pressburg.
6 August 1806: Francis ends the Holy Roman Empire.
14 October 1809: Salzburg goes to Bavaria.
14 October 1809: the Adriatic lands go to France.
14 October 1809: 'West Galicia was ceded to the Duchy of Warsaw'.
14 October 1809: 'Tarnopol district to the Russian Empire'.
14 October 1809: the Innviertel and Hausruckviertel go to Bavaria.
29 October 1813: Austria takes Trieste.
6 December 1813: Zara surrenders.
28 April 1814: Austria occupies Milan.
1814: the Palatinate passes to the Allies.
30 May 1814: Bavaria cedes Tyrol and Vorarlberg.
15 March 1815: Murat declares war on Austria.
20 May 1815: the Treaty of Casalanza.
9 June 1815: Austria takes back the former Illyrian Provinces.
9 June 1815: Lombardy-Venetia becomes Austrian.
9 June 1815: Ragusa in Dalmatia passes to Austria (same Final Act sentence).
9 June 1815: Austria regains 'Tarnopol district (from Russia)', ceded in 1809.
9 June 1815: Kraków becomes a free city.
9 June 1815: the occupation of the Illyrian Provinces ends in the Final Act (see the gain below).
9 June 1815: the occupation of Dalmatia and Ragusa ends in the Final Act (see the gain below).

9 June 1815: the occupation of Lombardy-Venetia ends in the Final Act (see the gain below); the kingdom is proclaimed in 1815 (Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia page: 'created in 1815 by resolution of the Congress of Vienna').
14 April 1816: Bavaria cedes Salzburg.
14 April 1816: Austria cedes the left-bank Palatinate.
1836: the Austrian army occupies Kraków.
1841: the occupation ends (same sentence).
16 November 1846: the Free City ends.
16 November 1846: Austria annexes Kraków as the Grand Duchy of Kraków (same sentence).
23 March 1848: Sardinia declares war on Austria after the rising of Milan and Venice.
March 1848: Venice rebels and holds out.
8 June 1848: Milan votes for annexation to Piedmont.
5 July 1848: Venice votes for annexation.
9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice returns Lombardy.
9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice returns Lombardy and Venetia.
By December 1848: Austria advances on Hungary.
20 March 1849: the war resumes.
23 March 1849: Novara.
24 March 1849: Austria occupies Lomellina and Alessandria.
13 August 1849: the Hungarian army capitulates.
22 August 1849: Venice falls and the war ends.
6 August 1849: the Peace of Milan.
1854: Austria occupies Wallachia.
1854: Austria occupies Moldavia (same sentence).
1856: Austria's occupation of Wallachia ends with the war.
1856: Austria's occupation of Moldavia ends with the war (same page).
26 April 1859: the Second Italian War begins.
12 July 1859: the armistice of Villafranca.
1859: Austria cedes Lombardy.
1 February 1864: Prussian and Austrian forces cross into Schleswig.
30 October 1864: the Treaty of Vienna ends the war.
30 October 1864: Austria and Prussia take Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg.
14 August 1865: the Gastein Convention.
1866: Venetia to Italy.
9 June 1866: Prussia invades Holstein.
20 June 1866: Italy declares war on Austria ('Italy declared war on Austria on 20 June'); the Battle of Custoza is 24 June.
June 1866: the Prussian armies enter Bohemia.

22-26 July 1866: the armistice took effect at noon on 22 July and the preliminary peace was signed at Nikolsburg on 26 July; the page does not say whether Prussia held ground in Bohemia or Moravia afterwards, so the contest ends with the fighting.
12 August 1866: the armistice of Cormons ends the Italian front ('the armistice of Cormons came on 12 August'); the Peace of Prague follows on 23 August.
23 August 1866: the Peace of Prague ends the war with Prussia; Holstein is lost.
23 August 1866: Holstein to Prussia.
30 March 1867: the Austrian Empire becomes Austria-Hungary.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Schönbrunn of 14 October 1809: Salzburg to Bavaria, the Illyrian lands to France, West Galicia to Warsaw, Tarnopol to Russia, a large indemnity and an army of 150,000.

wars.name: First Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Austrian victory: Custoza (25 July 1848), the Salasco armistice (9 August 1848), Novara (23 March 1849), the Peace of Milan (6 August 1849); 'Return to the status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
wars.outcome: Austro-Russian victory; Hungary under martial law, Vojvodina an Austrian crown land, Transylvania and Croatia ruled from Vienna.

wars.name: Crimean War
wars.outcome: Austria stays neutral, occupies the principalities 'for the duration of the war'; the Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Franco-Sardinian victory: Magenta (4 June), Solferino (24 June), Villafranca (11-12 July), Zürich (11 November 1859); Lombardy to Sardinia through France.

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Denmark cedes Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to Prussia and Austria (Treaty of Vienna, 30 October 1864); administered separately from the Gastein Convention (14 August 1865).

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussian-Italian victory; Peace of Prague of 23 August 1866 dissolves the German Confederation; Holstein to Prussia, Venetia to Italy.

wars.name: Neapolitan War
wars.outcome: Austrian victory: Murat declared war on Austria on 15 March 1815, was beaten at Tolentino (2 May) and the war 'ended on 20 May 1815, with the signing of the Treaty of Casalanza'; the Austrians entered Naples on 23 May and restored Ferdinand.

certainty.note: The Napoleonic cessions of 1809 and the occupations of 1813-1814 are treaty-defined, but the Cliopatria outlines are approximate until the Final Act of 9 June 1815.

Treaty and administrative borders after the Final Act; the Danubian occupation (1854-1856), the contested zones of 1848-1849 and the Holstein condominium (1864-1866) are exceptions, drawn by the ledger.
